key_insight: Integrating LungAI with Lung-RADS v2022 reduced cancers assigned to 12-month surveillance by 46% and benign biopsy referrals by 20% in the study analysis.
clinical_relevance: AI-derived nodule risk could help refine screening triage beyond size-based assessment, but improved patient outcomes remain unproven.
method: Validated LungAI on 2,747 held-out NLST CT examinations from 1,244 patients, including 89 cancers.
Compared performance with Sybil, nodule diameter, volume, and radiologist-assigned Lung-RADS v2022.
Applied prespecified AI score cutpoints to reclassify Lung-RADS pathways; separately evaluated a locked follow-up configuration.
evidence_signal: LungAI achieved AUROC 0.92 (95% CI 0.88–0.95); versus Lung-RADS on a weighted annotated subset, AUPRC improved significantly but AUROC did not.
watch_item: LungAI is investigational and not FDA-cleared; triage estimates relied on a weighted, cancer-enriched subset rather than prospective clinical deployment.
paper_title: LungAI: An AI Biomarker that Refines Lung-RADS v2022 Triage of Screen-Detected Pulmonary Nodules
